topic.subject: physics
topic.title: Resistance in series and parallel circuits
topic.scopeBasis: TGS 2025-26: series/parallel voltage and current; TGS 2026-27: resistance
topic.overview: Resistance describes how strongly a component opposes current. It depends on the component and on circuit arrangement, allowing circuit behaviour to be designed and controlled.
learningGoals: Recall the precise Year 8 scientific vocabulary and symbols.
Apply the idea to an unfamiliar example rather than relying on recognition.
Use the command word, show working where needed and include every mark point.
mustMemoriseRules: Resistance is opposition to current and is measured in ohms (Ω).
For an ohmic calculation, resistance = potential difference / current: R = V / I.
Adding resistors in series increases total resistance; series resistance values add.
Adding another parallel branch gives charge another path and reduces total resistance.
For the same material and thickness, a longer wire has greater resistance.
For the same material and length, a thicker wire has lower resistance.
Resistance can depend on material and temperature.
A fair wire investigation changes one dimension while controlling material, temperature and the other dimensions.

mustMemoriseVocabulary.meaning: component whose resistance can be adjusted
material through which charge can move readily
sum of resistance values in one path
an alternative conducting path between junctions
unintended very-low-resistance path carrying large current

workedExamples.prompt: A component has 6 V across it and 0.50 A through it. Find resistance.
Find total resistance of 4 Ω, 7 Ω and 9 Ω in series.

practicals.title: Resistance of a wire
practicals.aim: Investigate how wire length affects resistance.
practicals.variables: IV: wire length; DV: calculated R from V/I; controls: material, diameter, temperature and supply setting.
practicals.method: Use a low-voltage circuit, select measured lengths of the same wire, record V and I, calculate R, repeat and plot R against length.
practicals.expectedResult: Resistance increases approximately in proportion to length for a uniform wire kept at similar temperature.
practicals.safety: Use low current, switch off between readings and do not touch hot wire.
practicals.evaluation: Use crocodile clips at measured marks, monitor heating, repeat and use a best-fit line.

commonMistakes: Multiplying V by I to find resistance.
Saying an extra parallel branch increases total resistance.
Changing wire length and thickness together.
examTips: Series means more obstacle in one path; parallel means another path.
When comparing wires, name every controlled property.
beforeStartingPractice: Read the key rules once, cover them, then retrieve them aloud or in writing.
Use MC first for confidence, but finish with typed, calculation, practical or explanation evidence.
After an error, study the explanation; the same concept returns later in a different format and again after 2 and 7 days.

practicals.subject: physics
practicals.topic: Resistance in series and parallel circuits
practicals.title: Resistance of a wire
practicals.aim: Investigate how wire length affects resistance.
practicals.variables: IV: wire length; DV: calculated R from V/I; controls: material, diameter, temperature and supply setting.
practicals.method: Use a low-voltage circuit, select measured lengths of the same wire, record V and I, calculate R, repeat and plot R against length.
practicals.expectedResult: Resistance increases approximately in proportion to length for a uniform wire kept at similar temperature.
practicals.safety: Use low current, switch off between readings and do not touch hot wire.
practicals.evaluation: Use crocodile clips at measured marks, monitor heating, repeat and use a best-fit line.
